title: Dedicated capacity load certification workbench
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Build a repeatable, customer-facing workbench for certifying Dedicated capacity throughput guarantees and autoscaling behavior. The workbench (WaveForge) will standardize synthetic workload profiles, runbooks, telemetry collection, and an acceptance checklist customers and SREs can run together. It should support deterministic replay, tenant-noise injection, quantized model variants, and warm/cold path measurements.
background: Customers expect documented throughput guarantees and predictable autoscaler behavior when purchasing Dedicated capacity. Current ad-hoc load runs and spreadsheets are high-effort and hard to reproduce across regions, model families, and firmware/driver combinations. We need a consolidated harness that encodes best-practice probes and provides evidence for SLAs and onboarding signoff.
scope: Design and ship WaveForge: a CLI + orchestrator + telemetry collector for Dedicated throughput certification. Includes standard test profiles, automated run validation, and an artifact bundle for customer acceptance. Integrations: telemetry pipeline, Console dashboard, and CI job templates.
out_of_scope: Full integration with commercial customer CI, automated legal SLA signatures, and long-term archival of all raw traces beyond 90 days.
objectives: Provide a repeatable harness to validate throughput vs. latency SLOs across model variants
Enable controlled autoscaler experiments (scale-up/scale-down, burst recovery, cooldown jitter)
Produce customer-facing artifacts: run summary, golden telemetry traces, and checklist for signoff
Surface regressions from runtime/kernel/quantization changes before customer rollout
success_metrics: WaveForge run reproducibility: identical run-summary metrics within 2% across 3 repeats
Time-to-evidence: < 4 hours for a standard single-region certification run
Onboarding conversion: reduce manual SRE validation steps by 60%
Detection: >90% of known throughput regressions detected by harness in CI pre-release
test_profiles: Steady-state conversational: 1k concurrent user sessions, avg prompt 80 tokens, 95th latency target 250ms
Burst profile: sudden 4x qps spike sustained for 3 minutes, observe autoscaler response and tail latency
Microburst sensitivity: 10ms inter-arrival variance injections to exercise batching jitter
Cold-start/Kernel-swap: measure first-token latency after model swap and after node boot
Mixed-tenant noise: 70/30 distribution of noisy tenants with adversarial long sequences
harness_components: KV-warm utility to prepopulate cache and record eviction traces
Telemetry collector adapter (push to existing metrics/trace pipeline)
Result bundler: gzipped metrics + flamegraphs + run-report HTML
methodology_steps: 1) Choose certification profile and model variant; pin kernel/driver version
2) Run baseline warmup sequence to stabilize caches and JITs (10 min common workload)
3) Execute steady-state measurement for 30 minutes to capture throughput/latency distribution
4) Exercise autoscaler: induce controlled burst, validate scale-up latency and tail behavior
5) Inject tenant-noise and run regression scenarios to validate QoS isolation
6) Collect artifacts, run automated validation rules, and produce customer-facing evidence bundle
7) If violations detected, collect debugging artifacts and attach to an incident ticket following the triage template
acceptance_criteria: Run completes end-to-end using CLI recipe without manual intervention
Automated validations pass: throughput vs expected, p95/p99 within thresholds, autoscaler reacted within configured SLOs
Artifact bundle generated and uploaded to Console run-history for review
SRE/PM signoff attached to the run and stored as onboarding evidence
runbook_snippets: If p99 latency exceeds target during steady-state, capture kernel-livelock profile and escalate to runtime on-call
If autoscaler fails to scale within policy, mark run as FAILED and collect node-level logs, controller metrics, and policy snapshots
For intermittent regressions, re-run with deterministic seed and increase sample window to 60 minutes
customer_onboarding_notes: Share WaveForge recipe and run-report with customer during onboarding call
Walk through steady-state and burst tests; confirm customer workload mapping to a profile
Use artifact bundle as contractual evidence for initial capacity acceptance test
decisions: Ship as CLI-first experience to lower friction for SREs and early-access customers
Standardize on 30-minute steady-state window for baseline certification to balance runtime and signal
Expose autoscaler policy knobs in recipe but keep default safe and conservative for customer demos
open_risks: Resource contention in shared fleet during multi-tenant noise tests can produce non-deterministic signals
Driver/kernel upgrades may invalidate historical golden traces; need clear versioning
Large artifact bundles may hit Console storage quotas if not pruned
next_steps: Demo prototype to runtime and SRE teams and collect feedback
Implement telemetry adapter to ensure wf.* events flow to the metrics pipeline
Add golden-run regression test to pre-merge CI for runtime changes
notes: Keep run artifacts immutable and attach version metadata for model/kernel/hardware. Coordinate with Console team for run-history UI slot.
estimate_reasoning: 8 points: moderate integration complexity (orchestrator + telemetry), plus validation and customer artifact packaging
